summary: Provision tenant-scoped Slack hierarchy + Confluence indexer with approval webhook and retention hooks
description:
Issue summary:
Request to build an automated provisioning flow that creates tenant-scoped Slack channel hierarchies (department/team prefixes + subchannel namespace), automatically seeds a corresponding Confluence index page per tenant, wires an approval webhook (Jira) for non-standard channel creates, and enforces retention/archive hooks based on data classification tags.

Why we need this: currently teams create ad-hoc channels and separate Confluence pages with inconsistent metadata. This causes discoverability and audit gaps for regulated projects and increases overhead for Security/Compliance to review retrospective requests. A single automation will standardize naming, policy enforcement, and lifecycle.

Impact: improves discoverability, reduces manual review load on Security by ~40% (estimate), enforces retention for sensitive workspaces, and provides tenants with an explicit claim/ownership flow.

Request details / acceptance criteria:
- A Slack provisioning API that accepts tenant_id, team_owner, data_classification tag (e.g., public/internal/confidential), channel_type template (project, incident, standup), and optionally retention_window.
- On create, provision channel with naming convention: <tenant-prefix>-<team>-<purpose> and set channel topic to include a link to the corresponding Confluence index.
- Automatically create a Confluence index page under /spaces/TENANT-<tenant_id>/Project Index with seeded metadata (owner, tags, lifecycle dates, linked channels).
- If data_classification is confidential or retention_window > 90 days, trigger Jira approval flow (Jira ticket auto-created, approvers list from tenant metadata). Channel remains in a pending state until approve/deny.
- On approve, webhook updates channel state and Confluence index; on deny the channel is archived and requester notified.
- Archival/retention hooks: after lifecycle end date, channel gets archived and Confluence index flagged for review; automatic snapshot exported to audit bucket (S3) for tenant-scoped retention period.
- Audit logs for every provision action emitted to central audit topic (audit-automation).
- Integration tests and runbook (Confluence) documenting the flow and escalation path.

Constraints and non-goals:
- This ticket is only to implement the automation and necessary infra hooks; UI/console changes are out of scope.
- On-prem/private tenant special network/SCIM integration is out of scope for phase 1 (we will add an adapter later).
implementation_steps:
1) Review existing slack-provisioner library and identify extension points for tenant scoping and metadata.
2) Add Confluence SDK integration to create seed index pages and populate metadata.
3) Implement Jira approval webhook: create Jira ticket template and approver mapping.
4) Wire retention/archival task producer to audit-automation topic with S3 exporter.
5) Create integration tests in staging: happy path + approve + deny + retention expiry.
6) Draft runbook and Confluence page describing operations and escalation.
7) Security review for audit exports and retention handling.
8) Canary deploy to a single pilot tenant, collect metrics for 2 weeks, then roll out org-wide.
testing_instructions:
- Create tenant-scoped request via new API with data_classification=public: expect channel created and Confluence index present, no Jira ticket.
- Create with data_classification=confidential: expect Jira ticket created in 'Pending Approval', channel remains in 'pending' state until approved.
- Approve ticket: expect channel activated and audit log emitted.
- Deny ticket: expect channel archived, requester receives notification.
- Set small retention_window=7 days and validate archival job archives channel after lifecycle end and uploads snapshot to S3.
- Verify audit event payloads include tenant_id, requestor, timestamp, and action outcome.

investigation_notes: Slack API supports channel creation with topics and purpose fields; we can set topic to include Confluence link. No rate-limit concerns for pilot volume.
Confluence has an API for page creation, but we need to provision a dedicated service account for tenant-scoped spaces. Ops to request space template permissions.
Jira approval flow: reuse existing jira-workflow-bot, add approver group lookup from tenant metadata stored in internal 'tenant-registry' service.
Retention exports: audit-automation currently writes JSON payloads; implement S3 exporter to produce zipped mbox-like message bundle and hash-signed manifest.
Edge case: tenant with >5K channels. For these we should default to a single umbrella index and paginate child entries to avoid Confluence page bloom.
Risks: accidental mis-tagging could cause data to be exported with wrong retention; mitigate with a pre-approval validation and a manual review step for flagged changes.
resolution_notes: TBD - Implementation and pilot pending. Security review must pass before production roll-out. Runbook and telemetry required prior to org-wide enablement.
acceptance_criteria:
- API creates channel and Confluence index with correct metadata.
- Jira approvals gate confidential/long-retention creates.
- Archival exports snapshots to tenant-specific S3 location encrypted with KMS.
- Audit logs emitted for every lifecycle event.
- Runbook published and validated by Ops and Security.
